descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Demonstrations — Comparing Length, Mass, and Capacity (A10.1-A10.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.A10.1: describe different ways that objects can be measured
curriculum_expectations.A10.2: compare the length, area, mass, and capacity of objects using concrete materials

unit_overview: A 5-day Kindergarten unit on measurement (A10.1, A10.2) framed around 'Bigger, Smaller, Same!' — Max the Measure Moose and Tess the Tiny Mouse. Day 1 explores LENGTH (longer / shorter / same length). Day 2 explores MASS (heavier / lighter / same weight). Day 3 explores CAPACITY (holds more / less / same). Day 4 introduces non-standard units of measurement (cubes, hands, footsteps). Day 5 closes with a Measurement Carnival capstone where children apply all 3 attributes. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will compare objects by length, mass, and capacity using concrete materials, and describe different ways objects can be measured.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We compare LENGTH by lining things up. Longer, shorter, or same length.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare how long things are.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Max compares animal trails and ribbons; children sort by length.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We compare MASS by feeling weight or using a balance. Heavier, lighter, or same weight.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare how heavy things are.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Tess uses a paper balance; children sort by mass.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We compare CAPACITY by pouring. Holds more, holds less, or same.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare how much things hold.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Max and Tess pour water between cups; children compare capacity.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We measure with non-standard UNITS — cubes, hands, footsteps. Same object: many units.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can measure with cubes, hands, or footsteps.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children use linking cubes and hand-spans to measure objects.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We use length, mass, and capacity to compare and measure. We pick the right way for each job.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare and measure things in different ways.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children rotate through 3 carnival stations: length, mass, and capacity.

recurring_characters.name: Max the Measure Moose
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly moose who measures everything. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young moose with big antlers, holding a measuring stick. Cheerful, curious expression. Wears a small explorer's vest with measurement tools in the pockets.

recurring_characters.name: Tess the Tiny Mouse
recurring_characters.role: Max's partner. The 'small' character who shows comparison from the smaller side. Cameo Lessons 1-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small mouse with big eyes and a tiny tape measure. Stands beside Max to demonstrate big-vs-small. Wears a polka-dot bow tie.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: Less long. Doesn't go as far.
Has more weight. Pulls down more.
Has less weight. Pulls down less.
Find out how big, how heavy, or how much.

pedagogical_notes: Kindergarten measurement is concrete — children must HOLD and PHYSICALLY compare.
Direct comparison (line up two things) precedes indirect (using a tool).
Non-standard units are foundational — children measure with cubes BEFORE rulers.
Use the 'same' option always — children need to recognize equality, not just inequality.
Pair work matters: comparing reveals what 'longer' means more than seeing one thing alone.
canadian_context_notes: Canadian examples: maple leaves of different sizes, hockey stick lengths, lake vs pond capacity.
Use snowballs of different sizes for mass comparison.
Toonies vs loonies for small mass comparisons.
Tim Hortons cup sizes (small / medium / large) for capacity introduction.
